question: A candle maker began the week with 78 finished candles in stock. She made 29 more candles for a wedding order. A bulk retailer then took candles amounting to 8 times her stock for a regional order, and a national chain multiplied that new count by 7 for its own warehouses. A rival shop across town sold similar candles for 15 dollars apiece, unrelated to this shipment. The chain later returned 1818 candles that hadn't sold during a slow month. A dozen scented sachets sat untouched on a nearby shelf, playing no part in the candle count. How many candles did the candle maker have left?

Maria's bank account started with 71 dollars. She withdrew 53 dollars for groceries. She deposited 29 dollars from her paycheck. She withdrew 37 dollars for gas and 9 dollars for parking. Then she deposited 80 dollars. Finally, her account balance was multiplied by 9 due to an error correction in cents to dollars conversion. Her car insurance was 200 dollars. After all withdrawals and deposits but before the multiplication, what was her balance in dollars?

A researcher started with 108 data points. She added 26 points from new collection. She multiplied by 5 for analysis cycles. She multiplied by 8 for publication scaling. She subtracted 4984 citations for author correction (converting to adjusted data units). Throughout data collection, morning surveys, afternoon analysis, and evening documentation tracked progress. Her colleague contributed 12 data points separately. What was the adjusted data unit count?
A business started with 13 items. They increased 5 times. They added 57 items. They tripled. They added 68 items. Converting to bundles (assume 1 bundle = 10), how many items are there?

In the morning, a bookstore starts inventory day with 134 paperbacks on the clearance table. By midmorning, a returned box adds 11 more paperbacks. At midday, a bulk donation brings the total to 7 times what it had been. In the afternoon, a library sale contributes 30 more paperbacks. A dozen bookmarks were tucked into random copies that morning, though that number has nothing to do with the book count. By evening, a huge clearance rush sells off 961 paperbacks. Right before closing, a final donation brings the remaining stack to 6 times what it had been. Overnight, a restocking crew brings the table's total to 4 times what it had grown to. How many paperbacks are on the clearance table now?

A business tracked inventory with unit conversion. Starting with 239 items, early losses removed 79 (160 items). Morning restock added 47 (207 items). Afternoon delivery added 47 more (254 items). End-of-day adjustment removed 56 items. Converting to standard boxes of 8 items, this represented about 24.75 boxes. A branch location had 95 items separately. How many items remained?

A warehouse started with 188 boxes. They multiplied by 9 for the holiday season. They divided by 6 for distribution centers. They added 55 boxes per center. They added 79 more. They removed 334. How many boxes per center?

A manufacturer started with 168 units. They added 14 more from production. They multiplied by 9 for scaling. They multiplied by 2 for both shifts. They removed 3068 for a contract. The company employed 30 people. How many units for contract?

A supplier managed 72 orders. He added 78 from new customers. He divided by 6 for packaging batches. He multiplied by 8 for fulfillment capacity. He multiplied by 5 for weekly throughput. He divided by 4 for fair distribution (measured in weekly order batches). His colleague managed 12 orders separately. What was the weekly batch distribution?

An artist started with 127 paintings in inventory. By morning, they doubled their collection through creation. Then they multiplied again by 7 as a prolific week continued. They added 14 paintings from mentees. Finally, 460 paintings were removed for a major exhibition. A gallery downtown held 300 paintings but separate collection. How many paintings remain in studio inventory?

On Saturday morning Cara's bakery had 193 loaves on its shelves, which was more than Ben's bakery next door had baked, and it sold 176 loaves before noon. In the afternoon Cara sold 11 more loaves and dropped 1 loaf on the floor, which had to be thrown away. In the evening a customer returned 4 loaves that had been ordered by mistake, and Cara cut every loaf still on the shelves into 2 halves to sell at the night market. How many half-loaves did Cara take to the night market?

A child received 36 dollars from relatives. She spent 21 dollars on toys. She tripled her remaining money with a matching gift program. Then she received 50 dollars more. She multiplied her total by 5 for savings goal tracking. How many dollars in her savings goal was set?

A bakery began with 40 kilograms of flour and divided it equally between its 2 ovens, setting the first oven's share aside. A supplier added 18 kilograms to that share. Every kilogram in it makes 5 rolls, and the bakery counted the rolls. A cancelled order returned 41 rolls, and a second bakery sent over 43. The rolls were then split equally between 2 shops, and the shop on Mill Street took one of those parts. The bakery records its proving times in minutes even though the recipe cards give them in hours. How many rolls went to the Mill Street shop?

A builder began with 167 workers. He multiplied by 5 through hiring. He multiplied by 6 for crew size. He multiplied by 8 for crew-hours calculation. He added 29 from additional hiring. He multiplied by 3 for quarterly projection (measured in quarterly worker-hours). Throughout the quarter, morning site prep, afternoon construction, and evening planning tracked growth. What was the quarterly worker-hour requirement?

A factory had 12 units. They added 23 units in the morning. They added 38 units in the afternoon. They subtracted 71 units completed. They multiplied by 9 for expanded projection. Finally, they multiplied by 7 then by 8 for comprehensive multi-shift planning. Using a morning-through-evening schedule with one distractor, how many units total?

A factory processes 91 kilos of material daily. On day 1, it multiplies by 7 (637). On day 2, 58 more kilos arrive (695). On day 3, 34 kilos are removed (661). On day 4, 245 kilos are lost to spillage (416). On day 5, output is multiplied by 8 (3328). Finally, 2837 kilos are shipped. Morning shifts were heavy, afternoon saw losses, evening brought shipments. What is the remaining material?
A store had 56 items. They doubled inventory. They added 13 items. They removed 40. They removed 42 more. They removed 17 final items. How many items remain?

In the morning the recycling centre received 9 crates of glass bottles with 216 bottles in each crate. The delivery lorry is 10 years old. In the afternoon a volunteer brought in 3 bottles from her car and a cafe dropped off 47 more. In the evening the centre paid out the deposit of 8 cents on every bottle it had received that day. How many cents did the centre pay out?

A person had 161 books initially. They removed 15 through donating. They then doubled by multiplying by 2. They divided by 2 again for even distribution. Finally, 29 more books were added. Their friend had 300 books but separate collection. How many books do they now own?

A musician had 158 songs. They multiplied by 7 times. They multiplied by 7 times. They added 74 songs. They added 37 songs. Someone had a dozen songs. The total progressed. 100 songs elsewhere. How many songs?

A city zoo tracked its total number of visitors throughout opening day, starting with 128 visitors at the gate that morning. By midmorning, 49 more visitors arrived. By midday, 25 more came through the gate. In the afternoon, a school field trip multiplied the tracked visitor count by 8. By late afternoon, a second school's arrival doubled that count. By evening, a concert crowd tripled the tracked count once more. By closing time, a headcount correction removed 2171 visitors who had already left earlier in the day. How many visitors did the tracked count show at closing time?

There were 34 ducks on the village pond, which is 40 metres wide. 28 ducks flew off to the river. Then 10 ducks landed on the pond. 13 ducks walked off to the field, and after that 50 ducks arrived from the lake. Finally 26 ducks flew away. How many ducks are on the pond now?

A baker started with 59 loaves. They added 78 loaves in the morning. They multiplied by 9 for planning. They added 68 more loaves. They multiplied by 5 for shipment projections. A competitor's oven made 400 loaves but was unrelated. After adding the morning batch but before the first multiplication, how many loaves?

The Wednesday quiz team keeps all of its prize money in one tin. The tin held 195 dollars at the start of the season. After the first quiz the team added 66 dollars, and the second quiz brought in another 31 dollars. A raffle added 68 dollars to the tin and a member's donation added 20 dollars more. The quiz nights are always held in room 12 of the community hall. At the end of the season the whole tin was divided equally into 4 envelopes. How many dollars were in one of those envelopes?

A factory had 220 units. They doubled for capacity projection. They divided by 4 to allocate to sections. They multiplied by 4 to expand each section. Finally, they multiplied by 7 for comprehensive planning. Using a morning-through-evening timeline with the intermediate state, how many units are projected?
